91e53285dfee54a08f652a09e3840f60093c7be8.summary: Analysis of Fruitfly, a newly discovered Mac malware family. It conducts surveillance on targeted networks, including capturing screenshots and webcam images and gathering information about devices on the same network. Malwarebytes described it as seemingly targeting biomedical research centers. Its infection route is unclear. Evidence suggests it may have circulated for more than two years, possibly since the Yosemite release of OS X in 2014.

hedges: possibly for more than two years
It's still unclear how machines get infected.
The malware appears to have actually been in existence, undetected for some time, and seems to be targeting biomedical research centers.
Still other evidence suggests the malware has been in the wild for at least two years.
It's possible Fruitfly wasn't developed until much later and simply incorporated those antiquated components.
